sensor_concept: Insurer-subsidised no-probe hot-tub node (temperature, pump CT, cover reed, level float) feeding a maintenance-compliance score; owners who keep the tub circulating, serviced and drained on schedule get the hot-tub endorsement or a discount.
notes: filtered: hot-tub family - kept M-01 and M-03
fixes: c5: insurer owns the claims loss and has a product budget (precedent: insurers bundling LeakBot); c6: insurer distributes to every policyholder with a tub; c8: no chemistry probes; c7: no insurer-linked hot-tub telemetry found.

title: Supported-living providers can't prove hot water is safe in hundreds of dispersed tenancies, and scald prosecutions follow
problem: Supported-living providers for people with learning disabilities or mental health needs run hundreds of ordinary houses and flats with no on-site estates team. Bath and shower TMVs drift, get bypassed during repairs or are never serviced, and when a tenant is scalded the provider can't show temperatures were controlled (the parent's evidence includes a £135k housing-association scald fine).
who_suffers: Vulnerable tenants; support staff; the provider facing HSE/CQC action
buyer: Head of Property / Health & Safety Manager at a supported-living provider
industry: Supported-living and extra-care providers with dispersed properties
current_workaround: Staff handheld thermometer checks before baths, paper charts, annual or six-monthly TMV servicing by water-hygiene contractor, landlord repairs
sensor_concept: Clip-on outlet pipe temperature sensor at each bath/shower TMV with LTE-M (no tenant Wi-Fi), logging every hot-water draw's peak temperature; alerts when any draw exceeds 44°C or the TMV fails; monthly evidence pack and servicing-need flags.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c5: provider H&S/property head owns the prosecution risk and budget without NHS procurement; c7: Factorylab ClipR and Legionella vendors target estates with in-house teams, not dispersed tenancies; c1: housing-association and care scald fines from the parent's own evidence; c8: one clamp sensor per outlet, cellular so no tenant IT.

title: Farm semen flasks run low between AI company nitrogen rounds, and the herd's stored straws are lost
problem: Dairy and beef farms keep semen straws in LN2 flasks topped up by the breeding company's delivery rounds. Farmers are advised to dipstick monthly (ideally weekly) and to call when the level falls below ~15 cm. Flasks run dry when a round is missed, a top-up is skipped or the flask's vacuum fails, losing the farm's semen stock (including sexed and high-merit straws) and disrupting breeding. Rounds run on fixed schedules regardless of need.
who_suffers: Herd owners; AI company drivers making unnecessary or emergency stops
buyer: UK Distribution / Logistics Manager at an AI breeding company running LN2 delivery rounds; secondarily herd owners
industry: Cattle artificial insemination and on-farm semen storage
current_workaround: Farmer dipstick checks, fixed-schedule LN2 rounds by company 'Distribution Specialists', emergency top-up calls
sensor_concept: Load-cell base plate under the flask (weight = LN2 remaining) or a neck temperature probe, LTE-M with multi-year battery; feeds the company's route planner so drivers fill on need, and alerts farmer and company at low level.
notes: Leads: Genus 'Distribution Specialist' job adverts (deliver LN2 and semen to customers); FWI 'tips for ensuring cattle semen is stored safely' (dipstick monthly/weekly, call below 15 cm). Need straw values and flask failure rates.
fixes: c7: lab dewar-monitor vendors (Networked Robotics, CryoScout, Sonicu) don't sell to farms or breeding companies; c6: the AI company's drivers already visit every flask; c5: the AI company pays for wasted stops and owns the customer; c8: load cell + LTE-M, no lab IT or basement RF problem.

title: Equine and canine reproduction vets store clients' frozen semen in their own tanks and carry the liability when a tank fails
problem: Reproduction vets and stud farms hold client-owned frozen semen (stallion doses are high-value and irreplaceable once a stallion dies). A failed tank or missed top-up destroys it. Documented cases: a tank malfunction losing 1,600+ straws (lawsuit), a Holsteiner stallion's 212 units lost in a defective tank, and a US dog-semen bailment jury award of about $2.3m.
who_suffers: Breeders who lose irreplaceable genetics; the practice facing bailment claims
buyer: Practice Owner / Clinical Director of an equine or canine reproduction practice or stud
industry: Equine and canine reproduction clinics, studs and semen storage centres
current_workaround: Weekly dipsticking, LN2 deliveries, contract clauses disclaiming tank failure, manual logs
sensor_concept: Load cell under each storage tank plus a neck temperature probe, LTE-M; low-level and rapid-loss alerts; per-client custody log proving storage conditions for disputes and indemnity insurers.
notes: filtered: near-duplicate of R02-M-06 (frozen semen LN2 tanks)
fixes: c1: semen is client property with documented six- and seven-figure bailment claims; c5: the practice owner owns the liability and buys directly; c7: lab LN2 vendors don't target vet practices or studs; c8: load cell + LTE-M.

title: Hired cut-off saws and wall chasers run without on-tool dust extraction, and the contractor can't prove otherwise when HSE inspects
problem: HSE's Dust Kills inspections repeatedly find high-powered saws running without on-tool extraction or with poorly maintained extractors, leading to enforcement notices; RCS exposure causes silicosis claims and prosecutions. Hire firms supply M/H-class extractors with the tool, but nobody records whether extraction actually ran while cutting.
who_suffers: Operatives exposed to silica; contractors facing notices and claims
buyer: Contractor H&S Manager, sold by the hire firm as a hire-desk compliance add-on
industry: Construction trades hiring cut-off saws, chasers and grinders with M/H-class extractors
current_workaround: COSHH assessments, toolbox talks, supervisor observation, extractor airflow warning lights
sensor_concept: CT clamps on the tool and extractor power leads (or a vibration tag on petrol saws) plus a differential pressure switch in the extractor hose; logs cutting minutes with and without working extraction; BLE to a site gateway or LTE-M; per-hire report issued by the hire firm.
notes: Leads: HSE CIS69 on-tool extraction; Construction Management 'HSE finds many examples of poor practice in dust inspections'. Risk: extractors already have local airflow alarms (no record).
fixes: c7: the HAV tag market is crowded, but no incumbent proves extraction-in-use for silica; c6: keeps the parent's strongest asset (hire firms already bundle monitoring tags); c8: CT clamps and a pressure switch avoid the parent's vibration-validity problem; c2: daily use plus recurring HSE dust campaigns.

title: Equity-release lenders' security stands empty for months after a borrower dies or enters care, and water damage erodes value they guarantee
problem: Lifetime mortgages are repaid from the sale after the borrower dies or moves into long-term care, so the home usually stands empty through probate. Burst pipes and unheated winters damage it, standard home cover lapses after ~30-60 days of vacancy, and the lay executor may not buy unoccupied cover. Under the no-negative-equity guarantee, any shortfall at sale falls on the lender.
who_suffers: Lender (NNEG shortfall); estates and beneficiaries
buyer: Head of Servicing / Redemptions or Collateral Risk Manager at a lifetime-mortgage lender or its servicer
industry: UK equity release (lifetime mortgage) lenders and third-party servicers
current_workaround: Letters to executors, reliance on executors' insurance, occasional asset-manager inspections
sensor_concept: Postal 'vacancy kit' sent when a death or care move is notified: tap-connector pressure sensor (zero mains pressure proves drain-down; re-pressurisation alerts), indoor temperature node, optional meter pulse reader; LTE-M; lender dashboard plus an executor proof pack for the unoccupied-home insurer.
notes: filtered: unoccupied-property family - kept M-10 and M-29
fixes: c5: the buyer is a regulated lender with a servicing budget that owns the shortfall, instead of a one-off lay executor; c1: exposure aggregates across thousands of redemptions a year; c8: pressure plus temperature, posted and self-installed; c7: void-security firms don't serve lenders' post-death books.

title: Repossession asset managers winterise and inspect every vacant repossessed home; one missed drain-down becomes a burst-pipe claim on the lender
problem: LPA receivers and mortgage asset managers hold repossessed homes for weeks to months. Insurer conditions require periodic inspections and winter drain-down, and managers pay inspectors per visit. A system refilled by a trade, squatter or neighbour and then frozen means an escape-of-water loss (parent evidence: ABI average burst-pipe claim above £17k).
who_suffers: Lenders and receivers; buyers of damaged stock
buyer: Operations Director at an LPA receivership or mortgage asset-management firm
industry: Repossessed residential property and buy-to-let receiverships
current_workaround: Periodic contracted inspections, plumber drain-down at take-on, paper inspection reports
sensor_concept: Self-fit pressure sensor on a cold-tap connector (proves drained; alerts on re-pressurisation), room temperature node and door reed; LTE-M; portfolio dashboard producing dated inspection evidence between visits.
notes: Need receivers' inspection frequency and block-policy wording for LPA receiverships.
fixes: c5: professional asset manager with portfolio budget and per-visit costs; c8: three simple sensors with no hub install; c7: incumbents sell intrusion alarms/CCTV to social landlords, not drain-down proof to receivers; c9: kits redeploy continuously across the portfolio.

title: Specialist unoccupied-home insurers could replace fortnightly inspection conditions with a posted flow-and-frost kit
problem: Probate and unoccupied-home insurers require inspections at least every 14 days plus winter drain-down or heating, with dated records; Financial Ombudsman cases show disputes over whether conditions were met. The insurer bears escape-of-water claims and the cost of disputes, and policyholders (executors) find the visits a burden.
who_suffers: Insurer (claims and disputes); executors doing visits
buyer: Underwriting / Product Manager at a specialist unoccupied-property insurer or MGA
industry: Unoccupied and probate home insurance
current_workaround: Policy conditions, inspection log forms, claim investigations, FOS complaints
sensor_concept: Insurer-branded rental kit: tap-connector pressure (drain-down), temperature, mains-power sense and meter pulse; LTE-M; automatically evidences each condition; premium discount or relaxed visit interval for kit holders.
notes: filtered: unoccupied-property family - kept M-10 and M-29
fixes: c5: insurer owns the claims loss and has a product budget (precedent: Hiscox bundling LeakBot); c6: the insurer ships a kit with every policy; c7: no insurer-issued probate kit found; c8: minimal sensors.

title: Social landlords pay heating contractors to cap off and drain down every void, but nobody can prove the system stayed drained until re-let
problem: At the start of a void, the landlord's gas/heating contractor caps the gas and drains the system. Trades, squatters or neighbours then refill it; in a freeze it bursts (parent evidence: Wolverhampton's 630 burst pipes; ABI average >£17k), and insurers decline on condition breaches.
who_suffers: Housing associations and councils; incoming tenants delayed
buyer: Voids Manager at a housing association, sold through its void gas/heating contractor
industry: Social housing voids (typical 2-8 week voids)
current_workaround: Void inspections, void-security alarms and screens (~£35/week), periodic visits
sensor_concept: Tap-connector pressure sensor plus room temperature node, fitted by the gas engineer at cap-off (5 minutes) and recovered at re-let; LTE-M; per-void dated drain-down evidence and alerts on re-pressurisation or <5°C.
notes: filtered: unoccupied-property family; near R01-C-29
fixes: c6: the gas/heating contractor already attends every void; c8: two sensors instead of a multi-sensor security hub; c7: void-security firms sell intrusion kits, not drain-down proof; c5: Voids Manager budget and contractor billing per void.

title: Housing associations own culvert trash screens on their estates as riparian owners but clear them only after tenants' homes flood
problem: Where culverted watercourses run under housing-association estates, the landlord as riparian owner must keep screens clear. Blocked screens on such land have been named in Section 19 flood investigations (parent evidence: Tunbridge Wells HA case); tenants are flooded and disrepair claims follow, yet asset teams have no screen inspection routine.
who_suffers: Tenants; HA asset and repairs budgets
buyer: Asset / Compliance Manager at a housing association
industry: Housing associations with culverted watercourses on their estates
current_workaround: Grounds-maintenance visits, reactive clearance after complaints
sensor_concept: Float switch or tilt paddle on a post at the screen face (water above threshold = blocking), LoRaWAN/LTE-M; storm-ahead alerts from forecast data; grounds-contractor visit tag.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c5: HA asset/compliance manager with discretionary budget instead of LLFA procurement; c8: one float/tilt sensor instead of the upstream/downstream differential kit; c6: grounds contractors already visit weekly.

title: Church roof alarms are left unset after services and still signal over phone lines, so lead-theft cover is void when thieves strike
problem: Ecclesiastical requires an approved, monitored roof alarm for higher metal-theft cover, and the alarm must be active at the time of theft. Volunteer keyholders often forget to set it after services and events, and PSTN migration silently breaks dialler signalling. When conditions aren't met, payouts are capped (£7.5k-£10k) against losses of £22k-£400k.
who_suffers: Parishes; churchwardens; diocesan budgets
buyer: Ecclesiastical-approved roof-alarm installers (selling to PCCs) and diocesan or county-trust alarm schemes
industry: Parish churches with roof alarms
sector: Places of worship, community halls & charities
current_workaround: Keyholder memory, installer annual maintenance, occasional dialler line tests
sensor_concept: LTE-M/4G communicator wired to the existing roof-alarm panel's set/unset and fault outputs (dry contacts), with mains-fail and signalling-path sensing; logs 'set after each service', alerts keyholders if still unset at night; status report for the insurer.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c2: set/unset events happen every week, so value shows in a 1-month pilot, fixing the parent's rare-theft problem; c8: dry-contact communicator, no outdoor roof sensors; c6: sold through approved installers already maintaining these alarms.

title: A one-sensor, monitoring-only recorder proves the weekly sprinkler pump test ran, without touching life-safety controls
problem: BS EN 12845 and LPC TB203 require weekly sprinkler pump tests (diesel: 30-minute run) with records, and insurers bind cover with warranties. Logs are skipped or faked; the parent's multi-sensor kit failed on cost (several hundred euros) and on the risk of needing FM 1330 or LPCB approval.
who_suffers: Site FMs; insurers; occupiers whose claims are challenged
buyer: Site Facilities Manager, sold and fitted by the LPS 1048 sprinkler maintenance contractor
industry: Sprinklered warehouses and distribution centres
current_workaround: Insurer test cards filled by hand; contractor quarterly visits
sensor_concept: Non-intrusive node: CT clamp on the electric pump supply or accelerometer on the diesel engine block (run detection and duration) plus pump-house temperature; battery LTE-M; automatic weekly-test record and missed-test alert. No connection to the pump controller, so it is evidence only, not a control device.
notes: Need insurer acceptance of an electronic test log; optional pressure switch on the test line.
fixes: c8: one clamp or accelerometer plus temperature (BOM ~£50) instead of a multi-sensor kit, and monitoring-only avoids life-safety approval; c6: LPS 1048 contractors fit it on their quarterly visit; c7: OEM monitors (SPP FireEye, Peerless FireConnect) are brand-tied and unpriced.

title: Logistics landlords insure sprinklered sheds on condition that tenants test pumps weekly and keep pump houses heated, but see nothing between surveys
problem: In distribution warehouses owned by REITs and funds, tenants run the sprinklers under full repairing leases while the landlord's buildings insurance depends on systems being tested and maintained. A failed system turns a fire into a total loss (parent evidence: Primark ~£50m claim), and landlord risk teams have no portfolio-wide evidence.
who_suffers: Landlords and their insurers; tenants' stock and operations
buyer: Head of Asset Management or Insurance & Risk Manager at a logistics property owner (REIT or fund)
industry: Logistics real-estate portfolios (big-box distribution warehouses)
current_workaround: Annual landlord inspections, tenant certificates, insurer surveys
sensor_concept: Per pump house: run detection (CT or accelerometer), pump-house temperature (frost), sprinkler tank float level, reed tamper on main valve sets; LTE-M; landlord portfolio dashboard plus tenant alerts.
notes: filtered: near-duplicate of R02-M-15 (sprinkler pump test proof)
fixes: c5: landlord asset manager with portfolio budget and insurance exposure, resolving the parent's landlord/tenant split; c7: OEM pump monitors sell to plant operators, not landlords; c8: simple sensors only.

title: High-rise residential buildings must check firefighting lifts and essential firefighting equipment monthly and report faults unfixed within 24 hours — by clipboard
problem: Regulation 7 of the Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022 requires the responsible person in residential buildings of 18 m or seven storeys and above to run monthly checks of firefighting and evacuation lifts and essential firefighting equipment, keep records available to residents, and report any fault not fixed within 24 hours to the fire and rescue service. Faults between monthly walk-rounds go unseen.
who_suffers: Residents; firefighters; the responsible person facing FRS enforcement
buyer: Building Safety Manager / compliance lead for the Accountable Person at a managing agent or housing association
industry: High-rise residential buildings in England
current_workaround: Monthly walk-round checklists by building managers or contractors; FRS online fault forms
sensor_concept: Kit of simple nodes: reed or tilt on AOV smoke vents (closed after test, stuck open), reed on dry-riser inlet and landing-valve cabinets (tamper or theft), pressure switch on wet risers, dry contact from the firefighting lift switch and fault relay; LoRaWAN building gateway; monthly check record auto-generated; 24-hour fault timer that drafts the FRS report.
notes: Leads: legislation.gov.uk uksi/2022/547 regulation 7; gov.uk fact sheet on lifts and essential firefighting equipment; FRS fault forms (Manchester, South Yorkshire).
fixes: c4: named statutory monthly check plus 24-hour reporting; c5: Accountable Person/building safety manager under the Building Safety Act, funded through service charges; c8: reed, tilt and pressure switches; c7: no brand-agnostic multi-equipment evidencer found; c6: lift and fire contractors visit monthly.

title: Communal fire doors in residential blocks stop self-closing or get wedged open, and quarterly statutory checks miss it
problem: The Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022 require quarterly checks of communal fire doors (and best-endeavours annual checks of flat entrance doors) in residential buildings over 11 m. Doors with failed closers or wedges let smoke spread; FRS audits find them and issue notices, and the defect is invisible between checks.
who_suffers: Residents; landlords and managing agents facing enforcement
buyer: Building Safety / Compliance Manager at a housing association or block managing agent
industry: Residential blocks over 11 m (social and private)
current_workaround: Quarterly walk-round inspections, fire-door surveys, hold-open devices, residents' reports
sensor_concept: Reed contact plus accelerometer per communal door: measures time to latch after each opening (closer working) and flags doors held open beyond a set time; LoRaWAN gateway; quarterly check report and exception alerts.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c5: HA or managing-agent compliance manager with budget, instead of fragmented HMO landlords; c8: reed + accelerometer instead of the parent's custom panel sensing; c4: statutory quarterly check; c2: every door closing is evidence.

title: Fire-alarm maintainers could log every weekly HMO alarm test from the panel's relay outputs instead of trusting a paper logbook
problem: HMO licence conditions require weekly alarm tests recorded in a logbook; councils fine landlords and agents when checks and records are missing (parent evidence: Gateshead £42.3k). Grade A panels in larger HMOs have volt-free fire and fault relay outputs that nobody uses for evidence.
who_suffers: Tenants; letting agents and landlords facing civil penalties
buyer: Compliance Manager at an HMO letting/managing agent, sold by the six-monthly fire-alarm maintenance contractor
industry: Larger HMOs (3+ storeys with Grade A panel systems)
current_workaround: Paper logbooks, tenant-performed tests, optional ARC connection for a fee
sensor_concept: Mains or battery LTE-M/LoRaWAN dry-contact node wired by the maintainer to the panel's fire and fault relay outputs (any brand): logs each weekly test activation, faults and disablements; missed-test alert; licence-ready log export.
notes: Wiring to panel auxiliary outputs must stay BS 5839-compliant; confirm maintainers' appetite.
fixes: c8: replaces the parent's custom microphone/photodiode sensing with standard dry-contact inputs on off-the-shelf nodes; c6: the maintainer fits it at the six-monthly visit; c7: panel-maker clouds are brand-locked and Aico's gateway covers only Grade D.

title: Holiday-cottage agencies manage hundreds of owners' homes that sit empty between bookings, and nobody records frost protection or pre-arrival flushing
problem: Off-season and between bookings, holiday cottages stand empty. Insurers' unoccupancy conditions (heating or drain-down after a set number of days) and Legionella guidance for holiday lets (flush outlets after a vacancy) both apply, but owners are remote. Burst pipes force cancelled bookings and refunds; stagnant outlets put the first guests at risk.
who_suffers: Agencies refunding guests; owners; arriving guests
buyer: Operations / Property Care Manager at a holiday-let management agency managing hundreds of owner properties
industry: Holiday-cottage management agencies and housekeeping firms
current_workaround: Housekeeper changeover visits, off-season keyholder checks, paper flushing logs where they exist
sensor_concept: One node per cottage: ambient temperature, clamp-on pipe temperature on the cold main and a hot outlet (detects flushing and low use), tap-connector pressure sensor (leak or drain-down); LTE-M; agency dashboard flags cottages needing heating or a pre-arrival flush, linked to the booking calendar.
notes: filtered: unoccupied-property family - kept M-10 and M-29
fixes: c5: agency with an operations budget and multi-property scale instead of single owners or leisure trusts; c7: void-property and Legionella sensor vendors target social housing and big estates, not holiday-let agencies; c1: cancelled bookings plus escape-of-water claims; c8: three cheap sensors.

title: Pallet and packaging makers must prove every heat-treatment batch held 56°C at the timber core for 30 minutes, or exports are refused
problem: ISPM 15 heat treatment requires the wood core to reach 56°C for 30 minutes, and the UK standard references a probe in the slowest-heating part of the chamber. Small pallet makers with basic chambers rely on chart recorders or manual readings; audit failures mean loss of registration to use the mark, and non-compliant packaging can see export consignments refused or destroyed.
who_suffers: Pallet makers; exporters whose consignments are held
buyer: Owner / Production Manager at a pallet or wooden-packaging manufacturer with a heat-treatment chamber
industry: Wooden pallet and packaging manufacturers registered for ISPM 15 heat treatment
current_workaround: Chart recorders, kiln controllers on larger plants, paper batch records for auditors
sensor_concept: Wireless core-temperature probes (thermistor on a drill-in spike) at the slowest-heating stack positions plus chamber air temperature; LoRaWAN to a mains gateway; automatic batch certificate when 56°C/30 min is achieved; alarm if a probe lags; audit-ready archive.
notes: Lead: IPPC 'UK heat treatment standards' chapter (56°C/30 min core, probe in slowest part). Need UK registrant numbers, audit-failure data and incumbent HT loggers.
fixes: c4: international standard with national audit; c7: kiln OEM controllers serve large kilns, small HT chambers likely unserved (to verify); c8: spike thermistors + LoRa with mains available; c2: daily batches.

title: Small abattoirs' older electrical stunners lack the per-animal parameter recording the slaughter regulation requires
problem: Retained Regulation 1099/2009 Annex II point 4.1 requires electrical stunning equipment (other than waterbaths) to be fitted with a device that displays and records the key electrical parameters for each animal stunned. Older tongs in small red-meat abattoirs lack it; FSA official veterinarians enforce welfare at slaughter, and failures risk enforcement action against the plant.
who_suffers: Animals; abattoir operators facing enforcement
buyer: Owner / Plant Manager of a small or medium red-meat abattoir
industry: Small and medium slaughterhouses (sheep, pigs, cattle)
current_workaround: Observation records, mandatory CCTV in England, replacing the stunner
sensor_concept: Retrofit inline module on the stunner output: current transformer, voltage divider and timer logging current, voltage and duration per stun; local display; cellular upload; daily records for the OV.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c4: explicit statutory per-animal recording duty; c2: hundreds of events a day; c8: current/voltage sensing is cheap; c5: owner-operator buyer; c7: new stunners have recording built in, leaving a retrofit gap for older kit.

title: Joinery and sawmill dust extractors overfill and ignite overnight; insurers require daily housekeeping that nobody can evidence
problem: Wood-dust extraction systems in joinery shops and sawmills feed bags, bins and silos that must be emptied regularly; overfilled bins, smouldering embers drawn in from machining, and extractor faults start fires that destroy workshops. Insurers of woodworking trades may impose waste-removal and extraction-maintenance conditions (to verify), and DSEAR applies to combustible dust.
who_suffers: Joinery and sawmill owners; insurers; staff
buyer: Owner / Works Manager of a joinery manufacturer or sawmill
industry: Joinery manufacturers, shopfitters and small sawmills with dust extraction
current_workaround: End-of-day emptying by staff, 14-month LEV thorough examination, spark detection only in large plants
sensor_concept: Load cell or ultrasonic level on dust bins/bag frames, CT clamp on the extractor fan (run hours, left running), temperature sensor in the bin or filter housing (smoulder detection after shutdown); LoRaWAN/LTE-M; daily housekeeping log for insurer.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c8: load cell, CT clamp and temperature only; c7: spark detection (enterprise-priced) serves big plants, not small joinery shops; c4: insurer housekeeping conditions plus DSEAR; c6: LEV examiners visit every 14 months and could resell.

title: First-aid route services visit eyewash stations routinely, but the ANSI weekly activation is still the customer's blank paper tag
problem: ANSI Z358.1 (used by OSHA) expects plumbed eyewash and safety showers to be activated weekly; OSHA frequently cites 1910.151(c). Route services such as Cintas scan, inspect and tag stations on periodic visits, but the weekly activation falls to site staff and is skipped.
who_suffers: Workers with chemical eye splashes; EHS managers facing citations
buyer: Product manager of a first-aid & safety route service, or EHS Manager of multi-site US facilities
industry: US uniform/first-aid route services and their manufacturing and warehouse customers
current_workaround: Weekly in-house flushes with paper tags; route-service periodic inspection
sensor_concept: Clamp-on flow switch or pipe-temperature delta on the eyewash supply plus a reed on the valve handle; BLE read by the route driver's scanner and optional LTE-M hub; logs every activation (weekly test or real use) and alerts on missed weeks or real activations.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c6: route services already visit and barcode-scan stations; c9: route contracts are recurring; c5: the route company buys at scale; c1 remains the weak point (OSHA penalties only).

title: Marina fuel berths reconcile stock by hand, so a leaking pontoon line or tank shows up as a sheen on the water, not a number
problem: Marinas sell diesel (and some petrol) from tanks through pipework running under pontoons. Leaks and overfills go straight into harbour water, bringing pollution liability and clean-up, while stock reconciliation is a manual dip and totaliser read. Forecourt wetstock (SIR) services target road forecourts, not marinas.
who_suffers: Marina operators; harbour users and wildlife
buyer: Operations Manager / Harbour Master at a multi-marina group or independent marina
industry: UK marinas and harbours with fuel berths
sector: Marine – marinas, boatyards, small commercial vessels
current_workaround: Dipsticks, pump totaliser readings, periodic tank tests, visual checks for sheen
sensor_concept: Ultrasonic or hydrostatic tank-level sensor (above-ground diesel tank), pulse pickup on the dispenser meter, pressure transducer on the pontoon fuel line for an overnight pressure-decay test; LTE-M; daily reconciliation and leak alerts.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c7: SIR vendors serve road forecourts, marinas look unserved (to evidence); c5: marina groups have ops managers with budget; c6: marine fuel installers and tank testers visit; c1: harbour pollution clean-up (overseas fines found so far, e.g. NSW AU$158k).

title: Overheating shore-power sockets at marina pedestals start boat fires, and marinas inspect them only at the periodic electrical inspection
problem: Marina shore-power pedestals and boat leads run high currents in a wet, salty environment; corroded or loose sockets overheat and start fires that spread between moored boats. BS 7671 Section 709 sets requirements for marina installations, with periodic inspection, but hot sockets develop between inspections.
who_suffers: Boat owners; marina operators and their insurers
buyer: Operations / Engineering Manager at a marina group
industry: UK marinas and boatyards with shore-power pedestals
sector: Marine – marinas, boatyards, small commercial vessels
current_workaround: Periodic electrical inspection, staff walk-rounds, metered smart pedestals at some marinas
sensor_concept: Stick-on temperature sensor at each socket outlet and a CT clamp per pedestal feed; LoRaWAN gateway at the marina office; alerts on temperature rise relative to load; pedestal condition log for insurer.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c8: temperature + CT on LoRaWAN; c5: marina group engineering manager with budget; c7: metering pedestals record energy, not socket heating (to verify).

title: Pig and poultry units must test ventilation alarms and back-up systems every 7 days, yet the test is a manual tick and failures still kill whole houses
problem: For animals that depend on artificial ventilation, UK farmed-animal welfare regulations require a back-up system and an alarm that must be tested at least every 7 days (Scottish, NI and earlier Welsh texts), and Red Tractor requires evidence that alarms are regularly tested. Untested alarms or standby generators that fail in a power cut suffocate whole houses of birds or pigs.
who_suffers: Animals; unit owners and integrators
buyer: Unit Manager / Farm Owner of an intensive poultry or pig unit, or the integrator's technical manager
industry: Mechanically ventilated broiler, layer and pig houses
current_workaround: Weekly manual alarm test, paper records for Red Tractor, controller alarms with autodiallers, generator test runs
sensor_concept: Independent per-site node: dry-contact tap on the alarm output (logs each weekly test and real alarm), CT clamp on the standby generator (weekly run proof), backup house temperature sensors, mains-fail detection; LTE-M; Red Tractor-ready weekly log; escalating calls if an alarm goes unanswered.
notes: Leads: legislation.gov.uk SSI 2010/388 schedule; NISR 2012/156 schedule 1; Red Tractor poultry welfare standards. Check England's WOFA 2007 wording.
fixes: c4: statutory 7-day alarm test plus assurance-scheme evidence; c1: mass-mortality losses per house (to evidence); c8: dry contact, CT and temperature; c6: ventilation dealers, farm electricians and integrators visit; c7: controllers raise alarms but don't evidence tests.

title: Private HV substations at factories, campuses and hospitals get monthly visual checks on paper; overheating transformers and flooded switchrooms are found late
problem: Organisations that own private 11 kV networks must keep switchgear safe under the Electricity at Work Regulations, with routine inspections by Authorised Persons and insurer engineering inspections. Transformer or switchgear failure causes site-wide outages and costly replacements; partial-discharge monitoring is enterprise-priced.
who_suffers: Site operations (outages); engineering teams
buyer: Electrical Engineering Manager / Senior Authorised Person (HV) at a manufacturer, university or private estate
industry: End-user-owned HV substations
current_workaround: Monthly substation visits, annual maintenance by an HV contractor, thermographic surveys, enterprise PD monitoring
sensor_concept: Magnetic-mount temperature sensors on the transformer tank top (oil-temperature proxy), room temperature and humidity, door reed, water-on-floor sensor; LoRaWAN/LTE-M; monthly inspection evidence plus alerts.
notes: filtered: c8: partial-discharge sensing too costly
fixes: c5: named Authorised Person or engineering manager with a maintenance budget; c8: surface temperature, reed and leak sensors; c7: PD-monitoring vendors are enterprise-priced; c6: HV maintenance contractors visit annually.

title: Housebuilders' finished but uncompleted homes sit empty for months; frozen pipes and stagnant water hit the builder before handover
problem: Completed plots awaiting sale or completion, and show homes, stand empty, often through winter. Burst pipes before completion are the builder's cost and delay completions; outlets left unused for months need flushing before handover.
who_suffers: Housebuilders (repair cost, delayed completions); buyers
buyer: Regional Construction / Customer Care Director at a volume or regional housebuilder
industry: New-build housing developments (completed, pre-handover plots)
current_workaround: Site-manager walk-rounds, frost heating left on, drain-down of plots, pre-handover flushing
sensor_concept: Reusable node per plot: room temperature, tap-connector pressure sensor (leak or drain-down), clamp-on pipe temperature (flushing events); LTE-M; site dashboard; moved plot to plot until completion.
notes: Unverified: frequency and cost of pre-completion burst pipes; NHBC or HSE guidance on flushing new homes.
fixes: c5: housebuilder regional director with site budget, not a leisure trust or council; c7: void-monitoring vendors target social and commercial voids; c8: three cheap, redeployable sensors; c9: continuous plot turnover.

title: Hired hydraulic trench struts and manhole braces lose pressure between shift inspections, and small utility trenches have no load monitoring
problem: Utility, drainage and groundworks contractors hire hydraulic trench struts, manhole braces and trench-box systems. Struts can lose hydraulic pressure (seal leaks, ground movement, plant knocks) between the start-of-shift excavation inspections required under CDM 2015. Excavation collapses kill and injure workers; real-time strut load monitoring exists, but only on large engineered excavations (Senceive sensors, MGF and Groundforce portals).
who_suffers: Operatives in trenches; contractors facing HSE prosecution
buyer: Contracts / H&S Manager at a utility or drainage contractor, offered by the shoring hire firm
industry: Utility, drainage and groundworks contractors using hired hydraulic trench support
current_workaround: Start-of-shift and post-event visual inspections on paper, re-pumping struts, engineered monitoring only on big jobs
sensor_concept: Screw-on pressure transducer at each strut's hydraulic charging port with a small BLE/LoRa radio; LTE-M gateway in the site box or van; alerts on pressure drop; auto-logs evidence for the start-of-shift inspection; hire firm sees which struts leak.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c7: strut load monitoring is sold only for large engineered excavations, leaving small hired trench kit unserved; c6: keeps the parent's strongest asset, as shoring hire firms supply and collect every strut; c4: CDM 2015 excavation inspections every shift; c8: pressure transducer + BLE; c2: daily.

title: Coach, bus and plant-hire depots run private diesel tanks and pumps with no wetstock reconciliation, so leaks and theft surface as ground contamination
problem: Non-retail fuel stores at depots (coach and bus operators, plant-hire yards, hauliers) sit outside forecourt wetstock (SIR) services. Uncalibrated pumps, leaking lines and theft go unnoticed; the parent's evidence includes a coach operator's diesel leak (uncalibrated pumps, ~£43k remediation) and Environment Agency forecourt-leak prosecutions.
who_suffers: Depot operators paying remediation; groundwater
buyer: Depot Engineering / Fleet Manager at a coach, bus or plant-hire operator
industry: Private (non-retail) diesel installations at transport and plant depots
current_workaround: Fuel-management dispensing logs, dipsticks, annual tank tests
sensor_concept: Ultrasonic or hydrostatic tank-level sensor, pulse pickup on the pump meter, overnight pressure-decay test on the delivery line via a pressure transducer; LTE-M; daily reconciliation variance with leak and theft alerts; Oil Storage Regulations evidence.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c7: SIR vendors serve retail forecourts, and depot fuel-management systems log dispensing rather than reconcile stock or find leaks (to evidence); c5: depot engineering manager with budget instead of fragmented independent dealers; c6: tank installers and testers visit annually; c1: remediation costs.

title: Industrial gas suppliers deliver LN2 to small labs and clinics on fixed rounds, topping up full dewars while others boil dry
problem: Small labs, clinics and vet practices receive liquid nitrogen by scheduled delivery or exchange of portable dewars. Fixed schedules waste deliveries on full dewars and miss fast boil-off, and when samples are lost the supplier relationship suffers. Parent evidence: weekly top-ups recommended by fertility guidance and scheduled supplier deliveries (BOC Cryospeed).
who_suffers: Customers losing samples; supplier drivers making wasted stops
buyer: Cryogenics / packaged-gas Distribution Manager at an industrial gas supplier or its regional distributor
industry: Packaged LN2 supply to small labs, clinics and vet practices
current_workaround: Fixed delivery schedules, customer phone orders, dipsticks
sensor_concept: Load-cell base or clamp-on neck temperature on each customer dewar, LTE-M; feeds the supplier's route planning and sends customer low-level alerts; bundled into the gas contract.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c5/c6: the supplier owns delivery cost and the customer relationship and visits every site; c7: lab-monitor vendors sell to end users, not as supplier vendor-managed inventory; c8: load cell + LTE-M.

title: Milk buyers reject warm collections, and the farm can't show when its bulk tank stopped cooling
problem: Milk contracts and dairy hygiene rules require milk to be cooled promptly and held cold until collection. A refrigeration fault overnight warms the tank, the collection is rejected and the farm loses a day's milk; processors' field teams handle the disputes, and older tanks have no telemetry.
who_suffers: Dairy farmers; processors' supply teams; refrigeration engineers called out
buyer: Milk Supply / Field Services Manager at a milk processor or co-op (offered to supplying farms), or the dairy farm owner
industry: Dairy farms supplying processors (bulk milk tanks)
current_workaround: Tank controller display, driver temperature check at collection, alarms on newer tanks, engineer call-outs
sensor_concept: Thermowell or clamp-on temperature probe on the tank plus CT clamps on compressor and agitator; LTE-M; cooling curve per milking; alerts to farmer and refrigeration engineer; evidence log for collection disputes.
notes: c7 risk: newer tank controllers already alarm; need rejection costs and Red Tractor Dairy/processor contract wording on cooling.
fixes: c5: processor field team or farm owner holds the loss; c6: tanker drivers and dairy refrigeration engineers visit routinely; c8: temperature + CT clamps; c2: twice-daily milkings.

title: Property insurers' risk engineers judge sprinkler warranties from handwritten pump-test cards they know are often incomplete
problem: Commercial property insurers issue weekly pump-test cards and bind cover with sprinkler maintenance warranties or conditions precedent. Their risk engineers survey sites once a year and find cards incomplete or back-filled; impairments come to light only after a fire, and the claim is disputed.
who_suffers: Insurers paying or contesting large fire claims; insured occupiers
buyer: Head of Risk Engineering / Property Underwriting at a commercial property insurer or broker programme
industry: Commercial property insurance for sprinklered warehouses and factories
current_workaround: Paper test cards, annual risk surveys, warranties and conditions precedent
sensor_concept: Insurer-funded, monitoring-only pump-run node (CT clamp or engine accelerometer, pump-house temperature, main-valve reed) with a portfolio dashboard; missed tests trigger risk-engineer follow-up; premium credit for monitored sites.
notes: filtered: near-duplicate of R02-M-15 (sprinkler pump test proof)
fixes: c5: insurer owns the claim loss and funds risk-improvement devices; c6: risk engineers already visit and issue the test cards; c8: monitoring-only and cheap; c7: OEM pump monitors are sold to plant owners, nothing insurer-led found.

title: Licensed asbestos contractors must keep enclosures under negative pressure, but manometer readings are hand-logged a few times a shift
problem: Licensed asbestos removal uses sealed enclosures held under negative pressure by negative pressure units (NPUs). Loss of negative pressure (NPU failure, power loss, torn sheeting) releases fibres; supervisors note manometer readings by hand. Other jurisdictions mandate recording manometers, and firms are fined when negative pressure is not maintained (WorkSafeBC: C$80k).
who_suffers: Operatives, building occupiers and neighbours; licence holders
buyer: Contracts Manager / Licence Holder at a licensed asbestos removal contractor; offered by asbestos equipment hire firms
industry: Licensed asbestos removal contractors
current_workaround: Digital manometers read manually, smoke tests, supervisor logs, analysts' clearance inspections
sensor_concept: MEMS differential pressure sensor with a tube through the enclosure wall plus a CT clamp on each NPU; LTE-M; continuous tamper-evident log; alert on loss of negative pressure; record pack for HSE licence renewal and the client.
notes: c7 risk: data-logging manometers exist; UK HSG247 recording wording not confirmed (search found Minnesota's recording-manometer rule and the WorkSafeBC fine).
fixes: c4: licensed regime with HSE scrutiny at licence renewal; c2: every shift; c8: MEMS differential pressure + CT; c6: asbestos equipment hire firms supply NPUs per job (the parent's hire channel).

title: UK sites must flush little-used emergency showers and eyewash weekly for Legionella, but neither the flush nor real activations are recorded
problem: Plumbed emergency showers and eyewash stations are classic little-used outlets: Legionella guidance treats such outlets as needing regular (typically weekly) flushing, and EN 15154 test regimes expect weekly activation. Sites flush by hand with paper tags, and a real activation (someone injured, often alone) goes unseen.
who_suffers: Injured workers; EHS managers; water-hygiene responsible persons
buyer: EHS Manager / Legionella Responsible Person at UK chemical, plating, pharma or battery sites, sold via water-hygiene contractors
industry: UK industrial sites with plumbed emergency showers and eyewash stations
current_workaround: Weekly manual flush with tag or sheet, monthly temperature checks by water-hygiene contractor
sensor_concept: Clamp-on pipe-temperature pair or flow switch on the supply plus a reed on the valve handle; LoRaWAN/LTE-M; logs each flush and real activation; alerts on missed weeks and on real activations (possible lone-worker injury).
notes: filtered: near-duplicate of R01-B-04 (eyewash/shower flushing)
fixes: c4: ties the shower to a UK Legionella flushing duty, fixing the parent's 'only general COSHH' gap; c6: water-hygiene contractors already visit monthly; c9: weekly records retained; c1 still needs incident figures.

title: Park-home and holiday-park sites beside small streams flood with no warning, because national flood warnings mainly cover main rivers
problem: Many residential park-home and holiday-caravan sites sit beside ordinary watercourses and ditches, often with culverts or screens on site. These small, fast-rising streams generally fall outside national flood warning coverage (main rivers), so elderly park-home residents and holidaymakers are caught by night-time flooding and fire-service evacuations, while site licence conditions expect flood-risk sites to have warning and evacuation arrangements.
who_suffers: Park-home residents (often elderly); holidaymakers; site owners facing licence action and claims
buyer: Owner / Operations Director of a multi-site park-home or holiday-park group
industry: Residential park-home estates and holiday caravan parks beside ordinary watercourses
current_workaround: Wardens watching the stream in heavy rain, national flood alerts for nearby main rivers, site evacuation plans on paper
sensor_concept: Solar-powered ultrasonic or radar level sensor on a post or bridge over the stream (plus a float switch at the lowest pitch); LTE-M; staged alerts to warden and residents by SMS and siren; screen-blockage detection where a culvert screen sits on site; event log for the licensing authority and insurer.
notes: filtered: not in top ~50 at SORT
fixes: c5: a multi-site park owner holds the licence liability and an operating budget, unlike council LLFAs; c8: one level sensor instead of a dual-sensor culvert kit; c7: gap where national warnings don't cover ordinary watercourses (to evidence); c4: site licence flood conditions (to verify).
